_comment: Curated note -> axis mapping, authored judgment committed for review
(same precedent as data/blocklist.txt: open it and argue with it).
Loaded by fragrance_graph.notes.load_note_axes, which re-checks every
entry against 'SELECT DISTINCT canonical_note FROM fragrance_note_claim'
at load time and drops anything the corpus no longer carries.
Every entry below was checked exact-case-insensitive against that
query before this file was written; nothing here is a substring or
family guess ('amber' does NOT pull in 'ambergris' -- they are
different rows and stay different notes). Six candidates from the
original brief did not survive that check and are deliberately
absent: clove, sugar, chocolate, cucumber, sea salt, aquatic notes --
the corpus's fragrance_note_claim table has no canonical_note equal
to any of those strings (it has 'cloves', 'brown sugar', 'cocoa',
'aquatic accord' etc., which are different rows, not variants of
these words, so they are not silently substituted in here).
A note may belong to more than one axis (vanilla is warm AND sweet).
An axis absent from a request (or a request naming an axis not below)
subtracts nothing beyond the literal word typed -- see load_note_axes.

2026-08-17: boozy notes (rum, cognac, whiskey/whisky, bourbon) added to warm after 'side effect but too warm' kept rum in the profile; axis entries match by token containment, so an entry may claim corpus variants beyond its exact string.
